noteRef.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specPoints.text: describe the structure of the urinary system, including the kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra

primer.text: The kidneys do not work alone: they sit in a plumbing system that carries blood in, urine out. Two kidneys, two ureters, one bladder and one urethra make the urinary system, with the renal artery and vein attaching each kidney to the circulation.

lessons.title: The Urinary System's Parts
lessons.opening: Two kidneys at the back of the abdomen produce urine; two ureters carry it downwards; the bladder stores it; and the urethra finally releases it from the body. Each kidney is also plugged into the bloodstream through the renal artery, which brings blood to be filtered, and the renal vein, which carries the cleaned blood away.
keyPoints: The urinary system consists of two kidneys, two ureters, the bladder and the urethra.
Ureters transport urine from each kidney down to the bladder.
The urethra is the final tube, releasing urine from the bladder to the outside.
The renal artery supplies the kidney with blood to filter.
The renal vein returns the filtered blood to the circulation.

low.restatement: Kidneys make urine, ureters carry it, the bladder stores it, the urethra releases it.
low.analogy: Four stops on a one-way waterway: factory, pipes, reservoir, exit gate.
low.examPointer: Never swap ureter and urethra — the two tubes are the classic naming trap.

medium.restatement: Ureter joins kidney to bladder; urethra joins bladder to the world.
medium.analogy: A house with two drains: one from the kitchen (ureter), one main outflow (urethra).
medium.examPointer: Write the direction with each tube's name — 'from the kidney to the bladder' — to lock the pairing.

check.stem: Which tube carries urine from the kidney to the bladder?

options.explanation: The ureter is the kidney-to-bladder tube.
The urethra runs from the bladder to outside the body.
The renal vein carries blood, not urine.
The renal artery brings blood in for filtering.

check.stem: What does the renal vein carry?

options.text: Filtered blood away from the kidneys
options.explanation: The vein returns the cleaned blood to the circulation.
Urine travels in the ureters, never in veins.
That describes the renal artery.
Urea leaves via urine; nothing returns it to the liver.

check.stem: Where is urine stored before release?

options.explanation: The bladder is the system's holding tank.
The kidneys produce urine continuously; they do not store it.
The urethra is a passage, not a store.
The pelvis only funnels urine towards the ureter.

check.stem: How many kidneys and ureters does the urinary system contain?

options.explanation: The system is paired at those two points.
Each ureter serves one kidney; the counts match.
A single ureter could not drain both kidneys.
Humans have exactly two.

check.stem: Which sequence shows how urine travels through the system?

options.explanation: That is the one-way flow of the urinary system.
Urine starts at the kidney, not the bladder.
The urethra comes after the bladder.
The ureter follows the kidney, not the reverse.

check.stem: Name the four structures of the urinary system.
check.modelAnswer: The kidneys, the ureters, the bladder and the urethra.

check.stem: Which two vessels connect each kidney to the circulation?
check.modelAnswer: The renal artery, bringing blood in, and the renal vein, carrying filtered blood away.

check.stem: Explain why confusing the ureter with the urethra would break an answer.
check.modelAnswer: Because the two tubes sit at opposite ends of the system and carry urine in different stages: the ureter runs from kidney to bladder, the urethra from bladder to outside; swapping them reverses the direction of flow and loses the marks.

check.stem: Label a diagram showing a kidney, its two attached tubes and the storage organ, naming every tube with its direction.
check.modelAnswer: The tube leaving each kidney downwards is the ureter, carrying urine to the bladder; the single tube leaving the bladder is the urethra, releasing urine outside; and the renal artery and vein attach at the kidney's blood side, in and out respectively.

glossary.definition: The tube carrying urine from a kidney down to the bladder.
The tube carrying urine from the bladder to outside the body.
The vessel bringing unfiltered blood from the aorta to each kidney.
